newsitem.title: CANADA: CRICKET-PAKISTAN WINS SERIES IN CANADA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PAKISTAN WINS SERIES IN CANADA.

text.p: Pakistan won the fifth match and the Sahara Cup series on Monday when master slow bowler Mushtaq Ahmed ambushed India with his battery of baffling leg breaks and top spinners.
Mushtaq sliced through the Indian top order to collect five for 36 off 10 overs, his best performance in one day internationals.

India, chasing Pakistan's 213-9 off 50 overs, were a chance to win the deciding game in the five-match series until Mushtaq began reeking havoc on the spinner-friendly wicket at the Toronto Cricket, Skating and Curling CLub.
Sachin Tendulkar's team suffered two mini collapses -- three wickets for eight runs after they had looked solid on 62-1, then three for seven runs to be a spent force at 99-7.
They dragged it out before being dismissed in the 46th over for 161, handing Pakistan a 52 run victory and a 3-2 series triumph. India had held a 2-1 advantage going into Saturday's fourth match.
Mushtaq collected the player of the match award while another spinner, Indian vice captain Anil Kumble was designated player of the series.
Kumble, bowling mostly top spinners with the occasional leg break thrown in, bagged another three wickets on Monday to bring his total to 13 for the series at an average of 12.2.
But his efforts weren't enough to tame Pakistan on a difficult batting track.
Although Wasim Akram's side struggled at times, a solid but slow contribution from Aamir Sohail (44) and a rapid fire 43 from Salim Malik ensured they put together a competitive total.
India dropped their experiment of opening with wicketkeeper Nayan Mongia and had marginally more success with Ajay Jadeja.
He battled hard to stay at the crease with Tendulkar (23) as India put on 46 for the first wicket.

But at 62-1, Mushtaq picked up the wicket of Jadeja (20), then quickly thereafter sent Sunil Joshi (2) and Mohammad Azharuddin (2) back to the pavilion and Pakistan took a stranglehold on proceedings.
The match attracted another good crowd to the Toronto ground and the organisers declared the rain-interrupted series a success.
